subject: Performance SLO / VPC qualification follow-up - Acme Corp
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@acme.com>, Bob Singh <bob.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO / VPC qualification follow-up - Acme Corp

Thanks again for the call today - really productive. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can line up a deterministic performance qualification for Private/VPC deployment:

High-level SLO targets (from our discussion):
- Latency: p95 <= 150ms end-to-end for in-region traffic (goal); p50 ~40ms
- Throughput: sustained 300 req/s for the inference route (90% of traffic is text-generation, median tokens ~60)
- Concurrency: support for spikes up to 50 concurrent requests without degraded tail latency
- Streaming: support chunked streaming (server->client) with token-level flush; target first-byte <= 120ms for streaming responses

Network / deployment constraints you mentioned:
- Private VPC peering preferred, otherwise IPSec VPN to us-east-1
- Egress through Acme perimeter firewall (stateful)
- On-prem colo -> AWS VPN hop (single-hop today)

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Acme to confirm whether the 150ms p95 target is end-to-end (client browser -> inference -> browser) or only the internal backend->inference leg. This affects network budgeting.
2) Provide network topology (CIDR ranges, VPN/peering info, whether you have an AWS Transit Gateway) and any firewall/NAT/egress IP constraints.
3) Run the quick connectivity checks in the attached redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf (we included sample traceroute/iperf commands).
4) Schedule a test kickoff the week of Mar 20 - propose Tue 2028-03-20 10:00 AM PT.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf (PDF) - contains traceroute and iperf steps we typically ask customers to run.

If that all looks good I'll put together a short mutual action plan and loop in our infra engineer (Stephanie) for the test window.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
(jordan.blake@redwood.ai)

From: Alice Wu <alice.wu@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bob Singh <bob.singh@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / VPC qualification follow-up - Acme Corp

Thanks Jordan - good recap. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The 150ms p95 target we mentioned was intended as the backend->inference leg (we have an internal 25ms budget for microservice hops; front-end to backend varies and will be part of our end-to-end testing later).
- Topology: we run a private colo in NY (rack) that peers to our AWS account in us-east-1 via an IPSec VPN to a Transit Gateway.
- Egress: all outbound inference traffic must traverse our perimeter firewall - we do NAT and have a small set of egress IPs we can share.
- Internal latency budget: most of our pipeline enforces ~25ms between services; anything above that becomes risky.

We can run traceroutes and an iperf3 test on Monday. Can you confirm the packet sizes you used for your perf tests? Also, do you expect jumbo frames (MTU 9000) to be required?

I'll confirm availability for Tue 3/20 10am PT - sounds fine for now.

Regards,
Alice Wu
Director, Engineering
Acme Corp
alice.wu@acme.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@acme.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / VPC qualification follow-up - Acme Corp

Thanks Alice - quick technical notes and what we'd like to collect before the test kickoff:

What we need from Acme for qualification:
- Traceroute (mtr preferred) from your calling host(s) to our target egress IP(s) listed in the checklist. Please capture both ICMP and TCP traceroutes if possible.
- iperf3 test for 60s between your test host and our collector (we typically test with 1400B payload; we can adjust if you use jumbo frames).
- Confirm whether VPN is IPSec site-to-site (policy-based) or uses AWS Transit Gateway; if TGW, please share the TGW ID.
- Port ranges: we only need outbound TCP 443 from your side to our egress; however, if your firewall performs deep packet inspection, please let us know - DPI can increase per-packet latency.
- NAT behavior: are source IPs preserved or SNAT'd to a small egress pool? We need the egress IPs so our infra can whitelist.
- Jitter/loss tolerance: share any historical packet loss/jitter numbers you have. Our test harness will measure jitter; target jitter < 5ms for our p95 goal.

Example commands (attach results files to the Drive folder):
- mtr -r -c 100 -P TCP your-egress-ip
- traceroute -T -p 443 target-host
- iperf3 -c <collector-ip> -t 60 -M 1400

I attached network-test-instructions.md with exact collector IPs and sample commands. If you have an Ops Slack channel we should join for the test window, please add us.

Thanks - Stephanie
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
(stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai)

Attachment: network-test-instructions.md
---

Appreciate the quick responses - putting a short mutual action plan below so everyone is aligned:

Mutual Action Plan (MAP):
- By Mon 2028-03-19: Acme to run traceroute and iperf tests, upload results to Drive folder (Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cRedwoodAcmeTests).
- By Mon 2028-03-19 EOD: Acme to share egress IPs and confirm whether IPSec or TGW is in use.
- Tue 2028-03-20 10:00 AM PT: Test kickoff - Redwood will run synthetic traffic and capture p50/p95 across 3 runs and a streaming latency profile. Stephanie will be on the call to look at packet-level issues.
- Wed 2028-03-21: Redwood to share initial perf report and any recommended routing/peering changes (if needed).

Notes: if Acme's internal microservice budget of 25ms is strict, our p95 150ms internal target may be tight after allowing for network hops; we'll identify optimizations during the test (direct peering or bypassing DPI when possible).

Next: Jordan will send a calendar invite for the 3/20 slot and Marissa will follow up on contract timeline/next procurement steps (deal RDW-ACME-2028-019).

Thanks everyone - looking forward to the tests.

Best,
Jordan
